column11: ANCHOR, MEASURED: Polivy's first-line capture. (1) Polivy US 2025 net sales were CHF 688mm (Roche Finance Information Tool FY2025, asset_revenue_regions) x 1.205919 USD/CHF (ECB 2025 annual averages: 1.129983 USD and 0.937031 CHF per EUR) = $829.7mm. (2) A six-cycle course nets $110,435: 2025 Part B spend per claim of $19,510.12 x 6 = $117,061, divided by 1.06. One claim is one dose: in 2024, 1,616,227 mg over 10,844 claims = 149 mg, one 1.8 mg/kg dose. That gives 7,513 course-equivalents. (3) First-line share: Medicare claims were 3,924 in 2022, before the April 2023 first-line label, and 13,091 in 2025. If relapsed use held flat, first line is 70.0%, a lower bound. That gives 5,261 first-line starts. (4) Polivy is a course (d=1), so starts equal the stock. The pool is each year's eligible diagnoses, 19,046 x 0.62 = 11,809. Capture was 44.6% in 2025, Polivy's second full year, and on the fitted curve below (87.3% of peak at index 1) the peak is 51.1%. JUDGEMENT: a multiple of 0.25 gives 12.8%. For: a CD20xCD3 bispecific in place of rituximab, EU approval, and r/r FL response rates near 80%. Against: US entry around 2030 behind Pola-R-CHP, with Roche (glofitamab plus Pola-R-CHP) and AbbVie/Genmab (epcoritamab plus R-CHOP) running their own first-line CD20xCD3 Phase 3s. OLYMPIA-3 compares against R-CHOP, not Pola-R-CHP. Two US CRLs, and no US lymphoma sales force. Pool crowding: this pool (11,809) differs in size from zilovertamab vedotin's relapsed slice (3,809), so the solver does not pool them, which is right for different lines.

Logistic fitted to Polivy's first-line CMS Part B new starts, measured as claims above the 2022 relapsed baseline of 3,924: 4,017 a year for 2023 (2,812 over the 0.70 year after the 19 April 2023 approval), 6,920 in 2024, 9,167 in 2025, and 9,980 for the 2026 run rate (Q1 3,476 x 4, less the baseline). Best fit: k 1.30, midpoint 0.72 years after approval, which is -0.48 from the first full year. RMSE is 44 claims on a fitted peak of 10,578 (0.4%), but that is 3 parameters on 4 points. The book's Enhertu curve (k 1.08, midpoint 2.2), which zilovertamab carries here, fits Polivy at an RMSE of 2,784. Counter-argument: Polivy ramped fast because it was already used in relapsed disease. A new US entrant might go slower, and launch_ramp.csv's lower quartile (7 years to peak) is the alternative.

Against: FL patients often wait and watch or take a short R-benda course, and this is about 2.2 years of IV dosing with CRS step-up. CR30 is a surrogate. Surovatamig (0.55 -> 7,678) is solved apart because the solver pools only identical sizes. Combined claims of about 28% a year stay well inside the pool, so the ratio should sit near 1, and the defect noted on the DLBCL row (no carryover-0 rule in solve) means it could not bind anyway.
